groups.text: A class histogram after two zero zero zero zero requests shows what fills the heap: forty-three MB of byte arrays, and two zero zero zero zero cached responses nobody meant to keep.
It can't tell you who holds them.
A heap dump can.
It is a file with every object on the heap, and every reference between them.
J command writes one from a running J V M, or the J V M writes one when it runs out of memory.
Here is the graph inside it.
A static field holds the map.
The map holds a table, the table holds two zero zero zero zero nodes, and each node holds a key and a response.
Each response holds a two KB receipt.
A currency catalog, another G C root, holds a shared EUR string, which the responses point to as well.
An object stays alive while a path of references reaches it from a G C root.
The collector frees everything else.
Every object has two sizes.
Its shallow size is its own bytes, the header and its fields.
The map itself is only sixty-four bytes.
Its retained size is what would be freed if it went away.
That is the object, plus everything reachable only through it.
Cut the map loose, and the table, the nodes, the keys, the responses and every receipt become garbage.
The shared EUR string does not, because the catalog still reaches it.
Add it up.
two zero zero zero zero receipts at two thousand sixty-four bytes, keys at eighty, responses at thirty-two, nodes at thirty-two, and the table.
About forty-four MB, held by a sixty-four-byte object.
Every path from a root to a receipt goes through the map, so the map dominates the receipts.
EUR has a second path, from the catalog, so the map does not dominate it.
Eclipse MAT turns the graph into a dominator tree, sorted by retained size, biggest first.
For this dump, the map should sit at the top, with about forty-four MB.
Follow its path to a G C root, and it ends at the field that holds it: the static IDEMPOTENCY_CACHE.
In Java and in Kotlin, it is one line.
Every request adds an entry, and nothing ever removes one.
The histogram said byte arrays.
The dominator tree says this map, held by this field.
